history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: CSV row 2509 ('Maa Tara Temple', Tarapith) is the SAME temple as CSV row 1191 ('Tarapith Temple', id tarapith-temple-birbhum). Keep-or-drop/merge decision needed. Tarapith is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas and a Siddha Peeth: the third eye (some traditions say the eyeball) of Sati is believed to have fallen here when Vishnu's Sudarshan Chakra dismembered her body. Legend says sage Vashistha worshipped Tara here - on the Buddha's guidance, after 300,000 recitations of the Tara mantra she appeared as a mother suckling Shiva, then turned into the stone image still worshipped in that form. The present 64-ft '4 chala' Bengal-style temple (built 1818 CE by Jagannath Ray of Mallarpur; developed in the 19th century under Bamandas Mukherjee) is a red-brick stuccoed structure with a shikhara; the fierce four-armed metal Tara wears a silver crown and umbrella, with red kumkum on the forehead. It is a major Tantra centre: blood sacrifice of goats is the daily norm, the adjoining maha smasan (cremation ground) on the Dwarka river draws tantric practitioners, and Jivita Kunda tank waters are said to heal. The complex also houses Chandrachur Shiv, Bajrangbali, Maa Shashthi and Bamakhyapa temples (all rebuilt in the 2023 renovation). Coordinates reuse the temple-level coordinates from 1191.json.

town_description: Tarapith is a temple town in Rampurhat subdivision, Birbhum district, on the banks of the Dwarka river, about 6 km from Rampurhat; one of the most important tirthas for Bengali Hindus and a prime spiritual-tourism destination in eastern India.
